It must stop if the ssm-skill-test-cpu alarm fires.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
{"id": "8413aff7-5e71-44c2-89cf-4a8254287311", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "chat_title", "title": "Restart EC2 instances tagged ssm-skill-test with alarm guard"}]}

{"id": "3506037f-dee8-445d-bb6d-206f4ac5c9bd", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's the command. I haven't run it.

```bash
aws ssm start-automation-execution \
  --region us-east-1 \
  --document-name "AWS-RestartEC2Instance" \
  --target-parameter-name InstanceId \
  --targets "Key=tag:ssm-skill-test,Values=true" \
  --max-concurrency "1" \
  --max-errors "1" \
  --alarm-configuration "IgnorePollAlarmFailure=false,Alarms=[{Name=ssm-skill-test-cpu}]" \
  --parameters "AutomationAssumeRole=arn:aws:iam::<ACCOUNT_ID>:role/<AutomationRoleName>"
```

**What each part does**
- `--targets "Key=tag:ssm-skill-test,Values=true"` selects every instance with that tag in us-east-1. `--target-parameter-name InstanceId` passes each instance ID into the runbook.
- `--alarm-configuration` makes Automation watch the `ssm-skill-test-cpu` alarm. If the alarm goes into `ALARM`, the execution stops and no further instances are restarted. With `IgnorePollAlarmFailure=false`, the run also stops if Automation can't read the alarm. That's the safer choice for what you described.
- `--max-concurrency "1"` restarts one instance at a time. This gives the alarm time to fire between restarts. If you use a higher value, more instances will already be restarting by the time the alarm trips. `--max-errors "1"` stops the run after the first failed restart.

**Before you run it**
- Replace the `AutomationAssumeRole` placeholder with a role that Automation can assume. The role needs permission to stop and start EC2 instances. It also needs `cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms`, or Automation can't poll the alarm.
- The `ssm-skill-test-cpu` alarm must already exist in us-east-1.
- If the alarm is already in `ALARM` when you start, the execution won't proceed.
- Stopping on the alarm doesn't undo restarts that have already happened.
- This runbook stops and starts each instance. Instances without an Elastic IP get a new public IP, and instance store data is lost.

You can preview the targets first with `aws ec2 describe-instances --region us-east-1 --filters "Name=tag:ssm-skill-test,Values=true" --query "Reservations[].Instances[].InstanceId"`.

I can also tailor this to a specific role ARN if you share it.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
